metadata.title: Attention Is All You Need
metadata.authors: Ashish Vaswani, Noam Shazeer, Niki Parmar, Jakob Uszkoreit, Llion Jones, Aidan N. Gomez, Lukasz Kaiser, Illia Polosukhin

nodes.name: Sequence Transduction Encoder-Decoder Architecture
nodes.statement: An encoder maps an input sequence of symbol representations $(x_1, \ldots, x_n)$ to a sequence of continuous representations $\mathbf{z} = (z_1, \ldots, z_n)$. Given $\mathbf{z}$, the decoder generates an output sequence $(y_1, \ldots, y_m)$ one element at a time, auto-regressively consuming previously generated symbols.
nodes.statement_clean: Encoder maps input symbols to continuous representations; decoder generates output one token at a time conditioned on encoder output and previous outputs.
nodes.origin_citation: Cho et al. 2014; Bahdanau et al. 2014; Sutskever et al. 2014

nodes.name: Transformer Encoder Stack
nodes.statement: A stack of $N=6$ identical layers; each layer has two sub-layers: a multi-head self-attention mechanism and a position-wise fully-connected feed-forward network. The output of each sub-layer is $\mathrm{LayerNorm}(x + \mathrm{Sublayer}(x))$. All sub-layers and embeddings produce outputs of dimension $d_{\text{model}}=512$.
nodes.statement_clean: Stack of 6 identical encoder layers, each with self-attention and FFN sub-layers wrapped in residual connection plus layer norm; output dimension 512.

nodes.name: Transformer Decoder Stack
nodes.statement: A stack of $N=6$ identical layers. Each layer adds a third sub-layer (multi-head attention over the encoder output) to the two encoder sub-layers. The decoder self-attention sub-layer is masked so that position $i$ may attend only to positions $<i$, preserving the auto-regressive property.
nodes.statement_clean: Stack of 6 decoder layers with masked self-attention, encoder-decoder attention, and FFN sub-layers, each wrapped in residual + layer norm.

nodes.name: Attention Function
nodes.statement: An attention function maps a query and a set of key-value pairs to an output (all vectors). The output is a weighted sum of values, where each weight is computed by a compatibility function of the query with the corresponding key.
nodes.statement_clean: Attention is a weighted sum of values whose weights come from a compatibility function between query and keys.

nodes.name: Scaled Dot-Product Attention
nodes.statement: Given queries and keys of dimension $d_k$ and values of dimension $d_v$ packed into matrices $Q,K,V$, $\mathrm{Attention}(Q, K, V) = \mathrm{softmax}\!\left(\frac{QK^T}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right)V$.
nodes.statement_clean: Attention defined as softmax of QK^T scaled by 1/sqrt(d_k), times V.

nodes.name: Multi-Head Attention
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{MultiHead}(Q,K,V) = \mathrm{Concat}(\mathrm{head}_1, \ldots, \mathrm{head}_h)W^O$ where $\mathrm{head}_i = \mathrm{Attention}(QW^Q_i, KW^K_i, VW^V_i)$, with $W^Q_i \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}} \times d_k}$, $W^K_i \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}} \times d_k}$, $W^V_i \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}} \times d_v}$, $W^O \in \mathbb{R}^{hd_v \times d_{\text{model}}}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Run h parallel attention heads on linearly projected Q, K, V, concatenate, project back; here h=8 with d_k=d_v=64.

nodes.name: Position-wise Feed-Forward Network
nodes.statement: Two linear transformations with a ReLU in between, applied identically and independently to each position: $\mathrm{FFN}(x)=\max(0, xW_1 + b_1)W_2 + b_2$ with $d_{\text{model}}=512$ and inner dimension $d_{ff}=2048$.
nodes.statement_clean: Position-wise two-layer ReLU MLP applied identically at each position; inner dim 2048.

nodes.name: Sinusoidal Positional Encoding
nodes.statement: $PE_{(pos,2i)} = \sin(pos / 10000^{2i/d_{\text{model}}})$ and $PE_{(pos,2i+1)} = \cos(pos / 10000^{2i/d_{\text{model}}})$, added to input embeddings; wavelengths form a geometric progression from $2\pi$ to $10000 \cdot 2\pi$.
nodes.statement_clean: Add fixed sinusoidal position encodings of dimension d_model to input embeddings; even indices use sine, odd indices use cosine, with geometric wavelength progression.

nodes.name: Shared Embedding and Pre-Softmax Linear Weights
nodes.statement: Learned embeddings of dimension $d_{\text{model}}$ convert tokens to vectors; the same weight matrix is shared between the two embedding layers and the pre-softmax linear transformation. In the embedding layers, weights are multiplied by $\sqrt{d_{\text{model}}}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Tie input embedding, output embedding, and pre-softmax projection weights; scale embeddings by sqrt(d_model).

nodes.name: Self-Attention (Intra-Attention)
nodes.statement: An attention mechanism relating different positions of a single sequence in order to compute a representation of the sequence; in a self-attention layer all of the keys, values, and queries come from the same place (typically the previous layer's output).
nodes.statement_clean: Attention computed within a single sequence: keys, queries, and values all come from the same source.
nodes.origin_citation: Cheng et al. 2016; Parikh et al. 2016; Lin et al. 2017

nodes.name: Scaled Dot-Product Attention
nodes.statement: Compute $\mathrm{softmax}(QK^T/\sqrt{d_k})V$: form dot products of queries with keys, divide by $\sqrt{d_k}$, apply softmax, multiply by values.
input: Optional mask (for decoder self-attention): set illegal logits to $-\infty$
nodes.pseudocode: 1. Compute scores $S = QK^T \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times m}$. 2. Scale: $S \leftarrow S/\sqrt{d_k}$. 3. Optionally mask illegal positions to $-\infty$. 4. Apply row-wise softmax: $A = \mathrm{softmax}(S)$. 5. Return $AV$.

nodes.name: Multi-Head Attention
nodes.statement: Project $Q,K,V$ with $h$ learned linear projections, run scaled dot-product attention in parallel on each, concatenate the outputs, and project back to $d_{\text{model}}$.
input: Query, key, value tensors $Q, K, V$ of dimension $d_{\text{model}}$

nodes.name: Transformer Encoder Layer
nodes.statement: Apply multi-head self-attention, then position-wise FFN; each sub-layer is wrapped with residual connection and layer normalization: $\mathrm{LayerNorm}(x + \mathrm{Sublayer}(x))$.

nodes.name: Transformer Decoder Layer
nodes.statement: Three sub-layers: masked multi-head self-attention, multi-head encoder-decoder attention (queries from previous decoder layer, keys/values from encoder output), then position-wise FFN; each wrapped with residual + layer norm.
input: Causal mask preventing attending to future positions

nodes.name: Transformer (Full Model)
nodes.statement: Stack $N=6$ encoder layers and $N=6$ decoder layers; embed inputs/outputs and add sinusoidal positional encodings; project decoder output by shared embedding weights to predict the next token.
output: Next-token probability distribution at each target position
nodes.pseudocode: 1. Embed source and add positional encoding -> $X^{(0)}$. 2. For $\ell = 1..N$: $X^{(\ell)} = \mathrm{EncoderLayer}(X^{(\ell-1)})$. 3. Embed target prefix and add positional encoding -> $Y^{(0)}$. 4. For $\ell = 1..N$: $Y^{(\ell)} = \mathrm{DecoderLayer}(Y^{(\ell-1)}, X^{(N)})$. 5. Project $Y^{(N)}$ through shared embedding matrix and softmax to get next-token probabilities.

nodes.name: Adam with Inverse-Square-Root Warmup Schedule
nodes.statement: Optimizer: Adam ($\beta_1=0.9$, $\beta_2=0.98$, $\epsilon=10^{-9}$) with learning rate $\mathit{lrate} = d_{\text{model}}^{-0.5} \cdot \min(\mathit{step\_num}^{-0.5}, \mathit{step\_num} \cdot \mathit{warmup\_steps}^{-1.5})$, $\mathit{warmup\_steps}=4000$.
nodes.pseudocode: Compute lrate per the formula (linear warmup for first 4000 steps, then proportional to step^{-0.5}); apply Adam update with the given betas.

nodes.name: Scaled Dot-Product Attention Equation
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{Attention}(Q, K, V) = \mathrm{softmax}\!\left(\frac{QK^T}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right)V$.

nodes.name: Multi-Head Attention Equation
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{MultiHead}(Q, K, V) = \mathrm{Concat}(\mathrm{head}_1, \ldots, \mathrm{head}_h)W^O$ where $\mathrm{head}_i = \mathrm{Attention}(QW^Q_i, KW^K_i, VW^V_i)$.

nodes.name: Position-wise Feed-Forward Equation
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{FFN}(x) = \max(0, xW_1 + b_1)W_2 + b_2$.

nodes.name: Sinusoidal Positional Encoding Equations
nodes.statement: $PE_{(pos,2i)} = \sin(pos / 10000^{2i/d_{\text{model}}})$, $PE_{(pos,2i+1)} = \cos(pos / 10000^{2i/d_{\text{model}}})$.

nodes.name: Inverse-Square-Root Learning Rate Schedule
nodes.statement: $\mathit{lrate} = d_{\text{model}}^{-0.5} \cdot \min(\mathit{step\_num}^{-0.5}, \mathit{step\_num} \cdot \mathit{warmup\_steps}^{-1.5})$.

nodes.name: Variance of Dot Product Grows with $d_k$
nodes.statement: If components of $q$ and $k$ are independent random variables with mean $0$ and variance $1$, then $q \cdot k = \sum_{i=1}^{d_k} q_i k_i$ has mean $0$ and variance $d_k$.
assumptions: $q, k \in \mathbb{R}^{d_k}$ with i.i.d. components, each mean $0$ and variance $1$

nodes.name: Layer Complexity Comparison
nodes.statement: Per-layer complexity, sequential operations, and maximum path length are: Self-Attention $O(n^2 \cdot d)$, $O(1)$, $O(1)$; Recurrent $O(n \cdot d^2)$, $O(n)$, $O(n)$; Convolutional $O(k \cdot n \cdot d^2)$, $O(1)$, $O(\log_k n)$; Restricted Self-Attention $O(r \cdot n \cdot d)$, $O(1)$, $O(n/r)$.
assumptions: $r$ is neighborhood size in restricted self-attention
conclusions: Self-attention has lower per-layer complexity than recurrent layers when $n < d$
Self-attention has $O(1)$ sequential operations and $O(1)$ maximum path length, both asymptotically better than recurrent and convolutional layers

nodes.name: Linear Representability of Position Offset
nodes.statement: For the chosen sinusoidal positional encoding and any fixed offset $k$, $PE_{pos+k}$ can be represented as a linear function of $PE_{pos}$.
assumptions: $PE$ is the sinusoidal positional encoding with $PE_{(pos,2i)} = \sin(pos / 10000^{2i/d_{\text{model}}})$ and $PE_{(pos,2i+1)} = \cos(pos / 10000^{2i/d_{\text{model}}})$
conclusions: $PE_{pos+k}$ is a linear function of $PE_{pos}$, allowing the model to easily learn to attend by relative positions

nodes.name: WMT 2014 English-to-German Translation
nodes.statement: On WMT 2014 EN-DE, Transformer (big) achieves $28.4$ BLEU, surpassing the previous best (including ensembles) by more than $2.0$ BLEU; the base model also surpasses all previously published single models, at training cost $3.3 \cdot 10^{18}$ FLOPs.

nodes.name: WMT 2014 English-to-French Translation
nodes.statement: On WMT 2014 EN-FR, Transformer (big) achieves a BLEU score of $41.8$ (single model), trained on $8$ P100 GPUs for $3.5$ days, at less than $1/4$ the training cost of the prior state-of-the-art.

nodes.name: English Constituency Parsing on WSJ
nodes.statement: A 4-layer Transformer with $d_{\text{model}}=1024$ trained on WSJ Penn Treebank ($\sim 40$K sentences) reaches F1 $91.3$ (WSJ-only) and $92.7$ (semi-supervised) on Section 23, outperforming all reported models except the RNN Grammar.

nodes.name: Model Variation Ablations
nodes.statement: Varying $h$, $d_k$, $d_v$, $N$, $d_{\text{model}}$, $d_{ff}$, dropout $P_{\text{drop}}$, and label smoothing $\epsilon_{ls}$ on EN-DE newstest2013: single-head is $0.9$ BLEU worse than $h=8$; bigger models are better; dropout helps avoid over-fitting; learned position embeddings give nearly identical results to sinusoids.

nodes.name: Attention Visualizations
nodes.statement: Visualizations of encoder self-attention heads in layer 5 of 6 show heads attending to long-distance dependencies (e.g. completing the phrase `making...more difficult'), heads exhibiting anaphora-resolution behavior on the word `its', and heads whose patterns reflect syntactic structure.

nodes.name: Computational Cost Equivalence with Single-Head Attention
nodes.statement: Due to the reduced per-head dimension $d_k = d_v = d_{\text{model}}/h = 64$, the total computational cost of multi-head attention is similar to that of single-head attention with full dimensionality.

nodes.name: Three Uses of Multi-Head Attention
nodes.section: 3.2.3 Applications of Attention in our Model
nodes.statement: Multi-head attention is used in three roles: (i) encoder-decoder attention with queries from the decoder and keys/values from the encoder output; (ii) encoder self-attention; (iii) masked decoder self-attention preserving the auto-regressive property by setting illegal logits to $-\infty$.

nodes.name: Self-Attention Yields Interpretability
nodes.statement: Self-attention may yield more interpretable models: individual attention heads learn to perform different tasks, and many appear to exhibit behavior related to syntactic and semantic structure.

nodes.name: Dot-Product vs Additive Attention
nodes.statement: Additive attention (Bahdanau et al.) computes compatibility via a feed-forward net with one hidden layer; dot-product attention is identical to ours up to scaling. Both have similar theoretical complexity, but dot-product is much faster and more space-efficient via optimized matrix multiplication.

nodes.name: Restricted Self-Attention for Long Sequences
nodes.statement: For very long sequences, self-attention can be restricted to a neighborhood of size $r$ around each output position, increasing the maximum path length to $O(n/r)$ but reducing per-layer complexity to $O(r \cdot n \cdot d)$.

nodes.name: Regularization Recipe
nodes.statement: Training uses (i) residual dropout with $P_{\text{drop}}=0.1$ on each sub-layer output and on embedding+positional sums, and (ii) label smoothing with $\epsilon_{ls}=0.1$, which hurts perplexity but improves accuracy and BLEU.

nodes.name: Sequence Transduction
nodes.statement: Map a variable-length input sequence of symbols $(x_1, \ldots, x_n)$ to an output sequence $(y_1, \ldots, y_m)$, e.g. machine translation; the goal is to do so with high quality, parallelizable computation, and short paths between distant positions.

nodes.name: Compute scaled scores $QK^T/\sqrt{d_k}$
nodes.statement: Form $S = QK^T \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times m}$ and divide by $\sqrt{d_k}$ to control the magnitude of the dot products.

nodes.name: Apply optional causal mask
nodes.statement: If used in decoder self-attention, set entries of $S$ corresponding to illegal (future) positions to $-\infty$ so that the softmax assigns them zero weight.

nodes.name: Row-wise softmax
nodes.statement: Compute attention weights $A = \mathrm{softmax}(S)$ row-wise, producing a probability distribution over keys for each query.

nodes.name: Weighted sum of values
nodes.statement: Return $AV \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times d_v}$, the weighted sum of value vectors.

nodes.name: Linearly project $Q,K,V$ for each head
nodes.statement: For $i = 1, \ldots, h$, project queries, keys, and values via learned matrices $W^Q_i, W^K_i, W^V_i$ to dimensions $d_k, d_k, d_v$ respectively.

nodes.name: Run scaled dot-product attention per head
nodes.statement: Compute $\mathrm{head}_i = \mathrm{Attention}(QW^Q_i, KW^K_i, VW^V_i)$ in parallel for $i = 1, \ldots, h$.

nodes.name: Concatenate heads and project with $W^O$
nodes.statement: Concatenate $\mathrm{head}_1, \ldots, \mathrm{head}_h$ along the feature dimension and apply the output projection $W^O \in \mathbb{R}^{hd_v \times d_{\text{model}}}$.

nodes.name: Embed source tokens with positional encoding
nodes.statement: Look up source token embeddings (scaled by $\sqrt{d_{\text{model}}}$) and add the sinusoidal positional encoding to obtain $X^{(0)}$.

nodes.name: Apply $N$ encoder layers
nodes.statement: For $\ell = 1, \ldots, N$, set $X^{(\ell)} = \mathrm{EncoderLayer}(X^{(\ell-1)})$, producing the contextualized encoder output $X^{(N)}$.

nodes.name: Embed target prefix with positional encoding
nodes.statement: Look up target embeddings (scaled by $\sqrt{d_{\text{model}}}$), shift right by one, and add positional encoding to form $Y^{(0)}$.

nodes.name: Apply $N$ decoder layers attending to encoder
nodes.statement: For $\ell = 1, \ldots, N$, set $Y^{(\ell)} = \mathrm{DecoderLayer}(Y^{(\ell-1)}, X^{(N)})$ with causal masking on decoder self-attention.

nodes.name: Project to vocabulary and softmax
nodes.statement: Multiply $Y^{(N)}$ by the shared embedding matrix transpose and apply softmax to obtain next-token probabilities at each target position.

nodes.name: Self-attention sub-layer with residual + LayerNorm
nodes.statement: Compute $a = \mathrm{LayerNorm}(x + \mathrm{MultiHead}(x, x, x))$ where queries, keys, and values are all $x$.

nodes.name: FFN sub-layer with residual + LayerNorm
nodes.statement: Return $\mathrm{LayerNorm}(a + \mathrm{FFN}(a))$.

nodes.name: Masked self-attention sub-layer
nodes.statement: $s = \mathrm{LayerNorm}(y + \mathrm{MaskedMultiHead}(y, y, y))$, masking out future positions to preserve auto-regressivity.

nodes.name: Encoder-decoder attention sub-layer
nodes.statement: $c = \mathrm{LayerNorm}(s + \mathrm{MultiHead}(s, z, z))$ where queries come from the previous decoder sub-layer $s$ and keys/values come from encoder output $z$.

nodes.name: FFN sub-layer with residual + LayerNorm
nodes.statement: Return $\mathrm{LayerNorm}(c + \mathrm{FFN}(c))$.
